Y3n3c_8Nn2Y.title: fr-08: .the .product by farbrausch | 64k intro (2000) (720p HQ demoscene demo)
Y3n3c_8Nn2Y.summary: A recording of .the .product by Farbrausch, the first-place 64k intro at The Party 2000. It fits an 11-minute 3D demo with music into 64 kilobytes.
Y3n3c_8Nn2Y.why: HN commenters use it as the standard example of how much a tiny program can do, in contrast to bloated modern software.

quote.text: not very many 64Ks have reached the amazingness

PFUZlNQIndo.title: DuckDB – The SQLite for Analytics (Mark Raasveldt, CWI)
PFUZlNQIndo.summary: Mark Raasveldt of CWI presents DuckDB, an embeddable analytical database described as the SQLite for analytics, in a CMU Database Group talk. He explains why it was built, what it is for, and how it works.
PFUZlNQIndo.why: HN recommends it as the definitive talk from the implementer on DuckDB's motivation and design.

quote.text: one of the implementers giving a talk to CMU students about what DuckDB is, why they made it, and how it works

nIKhUizkXxA.title: DIY mass spectrometer measures potassium in dietary salt substitute
nIKhUizkXxA.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science builds and operates a simple mass spectrometer, using it to measure potassium isotopes in a salt substitute. He explains the design choices and the theory behind it.
nIKhUizkXxA.why: Recommended as an expert-made DIY build that explains why the apparatus is designed as it is, though one commenter notes a missing baseline run.

quote.text: he tries to explain why it's built the way it is and give you a good basis of the theory of operation.

5KiC03_wVjc.title: Sabine Schmitz's Nurburgring Van CHALLENGE | Top Gear - Part 2
5KiC03_wVjc.summary: In Top Gear's second part, racing driver Sabine Schmitz tries to lap the Nurburgring in a Ford Transit van in under ten minutes. She finishes just over the mark.
5KiC03_wVjc.why: Shared in threads about the Nurburgring and after Schmitz's death as a charming showcase of her skill.

quote.text: If you havent watched her take a van around the ring in a smidge over 10 minutes it is worth a watch.

E_F5GxCwizc.title: Native Advertising: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver (HBO)
E_F5GxCwizc.summary: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on native advertising, showing how ads are disguised as editorial content in news media, including BuzzFeed and major newspapers.
E_F5GxCwizc.why: Recommended as a funny, clear explanation of native advertising whenever sponsored content in media is discussed.

quote.text: I highly recommend taking the next 11 minutes to watch John Oliver talk about native advertising

PNbkv_DJ0f0.title: Ocarina of Time TAS by dwangoAC, TASBot, Savestate, Sauraen in 53:05 - Summer Games Done Quick 2022
PNbkv_DJ0f0.summary: A tool-assisted speedrun of Ocarina of Time at Summer Games Done Quick 2022, using TASBot and arbitrary code execution to reach an alternate ending in about 53 minutes. The run is introduced by its creators and followed by an interview.
PNbkv_DJ0f0.why: HN points to it as a stunning demonstration of arbitrary code execution in a console game and of what speedrunners effectively do as vulnerability researchers.

quote.text: absolutely blew me away

wROQUZDCIMI.title: Why Are Emulators Legal? Dolphin vs. Nintendo, and the Fate of Emulation [Great Emu War Pt. 1]
wROQUZDCIMI.summary: Moon Channel, run by a lawyer, explains the legal basis for emulation, including the history of emulation case law and Nintendo's takedown of Dolphin's Steam release. It argues the legality of emulators is more fragile than most people assume.
wROQUZDCIMI.why: HN points to it as a clear, lawyer-made summary during Nintendo emulator disputes like Yuzu.

quote.text: I really recommend folks watch this, from a lawyer

xUezfuy8Qpc.title: Rowan Atkinson on free speech
xUezfuy8Qpc.summary: Rowan Atkinson speaks against the word 'insulting' in the UK Public Order Act, as part of the Reform Section 5 campaign. He argues for robust free speech and against the slippery slope of criminalizing offense.
xUezfuy8Qpc.why: HN commenters point to it as an eloquent defense of free speech with concrete examples of the slippery slope.

quote.text: Rowan Atkinson explained it more eloquently that I ever could

4anAwXYqLG8.title: Sebastian Markbage: Minimal API Surface Area | JSConf EU 2014
4anAwXYqLG8.summary: Sebastian Markbage explains how React is moving toward a minimal API surface by leaning on language features and patterns instead of dedicated framework APIs. He also touches on JSX and syntax proposals for future JavaScript.
4anAwXYqLG8.why: HN cites it as a statement of React's early design philosophy of keeping APIs small and understanding JavaScript itself.

quote.text: I found this talk on the topic very interesting

TLm7Q92xMjQ.title: The simple, clever sensor behind automatic windshield wipers
TLm7Q92xMjQ.summary: Technology Connections explains how automatic windshield wiper rain sensors work, using an infrared light source and total internal reflection in the glass.
TLm7Q92xMjQ.why: Brought up in Tesla auto-wiper threads as the clear explanation of how simple conventional rain sensors work.

quote.text: Technology Connections has a good video on how traditional automobile rain sensors work

79fgH08z6xs.title: The History of 3D Graphics on the Gameboy Advance | minimme
79fgH08z6xs.summary: minimme traces the timeline of 3D graphics engines on the Game Boy Advance, from early experiments to commercial 3D games, covering techniques such as voxel rendering. It is a history and showcase of what developers coaxed out of the limited hardware.
79fgH08z6xs.why: HN people recommend it as the best overview of how 3D on the GBA progressed over the console's life, usually in threads about GBA ports and homebrew 3D engines.

quote.text: For a good overview of the progress of 3d GBA graphics over the console's lifespan I'd reccomended this video history

HNQ3GccCAI0.title: Crowd Wisdom Principles
HNQ3GccCAI0.summary: A ten-minute explainer from Hypermind on the wisdom of crowds, covering Galton's discovery and the diversity theorem. It argues that collective intelligence comes from diversity, independence and aggregation.
HNQ3GccCAI0.why: HN people cite it as a short explanation of how aggregated individual guesses approach the truth.

quote.text: A shorter explanation

JRcXUuQYR90.title: Mojo Lang - Tomorrow's High Performance Python? (with Chris Lattner)
JRcXUuQYR90.summary: Developer Voices interviews Chris Lattner about Mojo, a Python-compatible language aimed at CPU/GPU performance built on LLVM and MLIR. It covers performance features, the type system and why Mojo uses Python syntax.
JRcXUuQYR90.why: Pointed to as a general-purpose interview on Mojo's goals and design from its creator.

quote.text: Here's an interview with Chris Lattner discussing Mojo in much more generalized terms

KAm7qAKAXwI.title: How anti-theft tags work - magnetostriction
KAm7qAKAXwI.summary: Applied Science explains how retail anti-theft tags work. A tiny magnetostrictive strip acts as a mechanical oscillator excited by a magnetic field, and magnetizing or demagnetizing it arms or disarms the tag.
KAm7qAKAXwI.why: HN recommends it as an informative explanation of what those tags are, especially in threads about implants and RFID.

quote.text: here's an interesting and informative video from Applied Science on how these tags work

XFJnWp1tAdU.title: How to Surface a Submarine in the Arctic Ocean  - Smarter Every Day 260
XFJnWp1tAdU.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explains how a US Navy nuclear submarine surfaces through Arctic ice, filmed during the ICEx exercise. It shows ballast and control systems and the physics involved.
XFJnWp1tAdU.why: HN points to it as the best accessible explanation of submarine ice breaking and sub controls.

quote.text: this Smarter Every Day video is the best summary I have seen

ZI198eFghJk.title: Modernizing Compiler Design for Carbon Toolchain - Chandler Carruth - CppNow 2023
ZI198eFghJk.tz: Carbon 工具链的编译器设计现代化 - Chandler Carruth - CppNow 2023
ZI198eFghJk.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppNow 2023 talk on modernizing compiler design for the Carbon toolchain, using data-oriented design and modern hardware assumptions. It covers lexing, parsing and compact data structures aimed at compiler performance.
ZI198eFghJk.sz: Chandler Carruth 在 CppNow 2023 讲述为 Carbon 工具链现代化编译器设计，采用面向数据的设计和现代硬件假设，涵盖词法分析、解析和紧凑数据结构以提升性能。
ZI198eFghJk.why: Recommended as a recent take on rethinking compiler architecture, and cited in discussions of flattened ASTs and fast lexers.
ZI198eFghJk.wz: 因其对编译器架构的最新思考，被推荐在讨论扁平 AST 与高速词法分析时引用。

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: I recommend a watch of this for a recent take on trying to change how we think of these.

ZzsK8Am6dKU.title: Parsing with Derivatives
ZzsK8Am6dKU.summary: A Stanford talk by Matthew Might on parsing with derivatives, a new way to write parsers, and why better parsing tools are needed. It discusses language theory and criticizes ad-hoc hand-written parsers.
ZzsK8Am6dKU.sz: Stanford 的 Matthew Might 介绍一种基于导数的全新解析方法，解释为何需要更好的解析工具，并批评手写解析器的随意性。演讲涉及语言理论基础。
ZzsK8Am6dKU.why: Mentioned as a great talk and related reading in threads on parsing techniques.
ZzsK8Am6dKU.wz: 因为它是解析技术讨论中的经典推荐，提供了新颖的思路。

quote.text: he also gave a great talk on parsing with derivatives

IACHfKmZMr8.title: Vibe Coding Is The Future
IACHfKmZMr8.summary: A Y Combinator video on vibe coding, the term Andrej Karpathy coined for letting LLMs write code. It reports what YC founders say about debugging, models and how much of their code is AI-written.
IACHfKmZMr8.why: HN mostly cites it critically, as a source for the claim that much of YC code is AI-written and as an example of insiders promoting vibe coding.

pQQTScuApWk.title: Lucid Energize Demo VHS 1993
pQQTScuApWk.summary: A 1993 VHS demo of Lucid Energize, a database-backed, incremental C/C++ programming environment built on XEmacs. It shows features like incremental compilation, live debugging and hyperlinked output.
